title: Inheritance
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of inheritance and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—the extends keyword—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study inheritance with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you choose between inheritance, interfaces, and composition based on the relationship being modeled. In this lesson, focus on the extends keyword and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Inheritance models a substitutable “is-a” relationship, interfaces define contracts, and composition connects collaborators. Polymorphic calls use the runtime object’s override rather than the reference variable’s declared class. Apply that reasoning specifically to the extends keyword and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect the extends keyword with parent and child classes before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Parent and child classes
items.text: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance. Encapsulation protects invariants by keeping mutable state private and validating updates through a small public API.

items.title: Inherited fields and methods
items.text: A method gives a named contract to a unit of behavior. Keep responsibilities focused, define clear parameter and return types, and test typical, boundary, and invalid cases independently.

items.title: Designing useful inheritance relationships
items.text: Use inheritance for a genuine substitutable relationship, interfaces to express contracts, and composition to combine collaborators. Dynamic dispatch selects an overridden instance method based on the runtime object.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
